name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
description: Hold the kettlebell upside-down (bottoms-up) — bell balanced above a vertical forearm, gripping the handle HARD. Press it up keeping the bell balanced, like a string is pulling the base to the ceiling, then lower under control. The off-balance load forces the rotator cuff, grip, and a packed shoulder to stabilize, which is why it's a premier shoulder-prep / rehab drill. Go light, low reps, single-arm; balance quality over rep count. The two press planes bias different muscles: the "forward press" (elbow/arm kept in front, pressing straight overhead) loads the anterior deltoid + serratus in a stable line; the "T-press" (arm tracking out toward a T at shoulder height) shifts to the lateral/rear delt and demands far more rotator cuff because the arm is abducted. Keep the T-plane lighter — abducted-and-loaded is the more provocative angle for a cranky shoulder.
